game.name: Risk of Rain 2
game.short_description: Escape a chaotic alien planet by fighting through hordes of frenzied monsters – with your friends, or on your own. Combine loot in surprising ways and master each character until you become the havoc you feared upon your first crash landing.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Risk of Rain 2 is the 3D third-person shooter sequel to the 2D original, widely popular and heavily updated with patches and DLC. He loves it: the core shooting is so fun that it never gets old even though runs start fairly similarly. The constant stream of items keeps the character feeling steadily stronger. He places it in S tier, noting he plays it less these days than Peglin or Ravenous-style favourites, but it still earns the top spot.
praise: Core gameplay is so enjoyable it does not get old despite few starting customizations
Constant item drops (roughly five to ten per level) keep the player feeling rewarded and increasingly powerful
Huge item pool means steady power growth with core abilities even if individual items are not game-changing
The jump from 2D to 3D works amazingly well as a shooter
Many secrets, areas, biomes and bosses to discover
Varied characters with slight ability customization at the start
Visually pleasing, great multiplayer, and lots of updates and DLC
criticism: Runs start fairly similarly from run to run with few early customizations
Many items do not drastically change gameplay
unique_points: Rare case of a sequel moving from 2D to 3D successfully
Always-flowing reward loop from items compensates for limited starting variety
Easy to pick up, hard to master
commentary.quote: it's going to be an easy S tier for me
design_criteria: Core gameplay feel: fun enough to carry the game on its own
Item frequency and rewards: constant drops drive a sense of power growth
Item diversity: large pool, though individually modest
Starting variety: limited, but judged not to matter
Content and exploration: secrets, biomes, bosses
Accessibility: easy to play, hard to master
Level length: levels last several minutes
Visuals and multiplayer: noted as positives but not affecting the rating
commentary.rerank_note: Rated with the new content and DLC factored in; no explicit move from a prior tier stated.

community.one_liner: A 3D third-person co-op action roguelite by Hopoo Games in which you fight through escalating waves on an alien planet, stacking hundreds of items into absurd power builds before the difficulty clock overwhelms you.
community.consensus_summary: Risk of Rain 2 is widely regarded as one of the defining action roguelites: Steam lists it at about 94% positive across roughly 353k reviews, Metacritic critics give it 85, and outlets called it among the best roguelikes, especially in co-op. Praise centers on the item-stacking power fantasy, the character roster and the soundtrack. It left early access (March 2019) for 1.0 in August 2020 and has kept receiving paid expansions (Survivors of the Void 2022, Seekers of the Storm 2024, Alloyed Collective Nov 2025). The main friction today is less the game than its ownership: after Gearbox bought the IP in 2022 and 2K/Take-Two's EULA (mandatory arbitration) was added, many long-time players leave negative reviews while still praising gameplay.
best_things: Item stacking snowballs builds from a plain pistol into screen-filling chain reactions; the power-fantasy and 'one more run' loop is the core praise
Huge item pool and synergies reward experimentation and produce very different runs
Survivor roster plays distinctly, each with unlockable skill variants and alternate loadouts that add mastery depth
Co-op with friends (up to 4) is cited as the best way to play and the main reason people buy it
Stylish cel-shaded look and a widely loved soundtrack
Difficulty scales continuously in real time, so pacing and risk/reward (when to open chests versus finish the stage) stay tense
Lots of unlockables, artifacts, Eclipse difficulties and mods give hundreds of hours of replay; reviewers report 100-300+ hours
Post-launch support over several years, with Alloyed Collective seen by some as repairing the goodwill lost by Seekers of the Storm
worst_things: One-shot deaths from enemies or bosses (Brass Contraption, Elder Lemurian, Void Reavers) feel unfair when you are otherwise stacked with defence
Late-game screens fill with particles and effects until they are unreadable, and huge item counts can tank FPS
Repetitive environments and limited story, which critics flagged in reviews
Enemy variety feels thin to some players, and runs can feel like searching for the teleporter
Multiplayer desyncs, lobby failures and mid-run crashes reported since the Gearbox-era updates, with no reconnect option
Gearbox/2K ownership: a later EULA with mandatory arbitration and the console-port codebase drove waves of negative Steam reviews despite high playtime
Seekers of the Storm launched buggy and unbalanced (DLC alone sits around 54% positive on Steam)
No mid-run save, so long runs are all-or-nothing
improvements: Reduce or add options to tone down visual clutter and performance drops in late-game item-heavy runs
Better onboarding: new players report struggling to find the teleporter and learn mechanics, and only discover helper settings by accident
Fix long-standing multiplayer desync, lobby and reconnect issues
Add mid-run saving or suspend to support 1-2 hour runs
Address one-shot mechanics and tune balance so defence builds are not negated by single attacks
Revert or clarify the EULA changes and give players a way to report bugs in-game
unique_things: 3D third-person shooter take on a roguelite, unlike 2D top-down peers like Isaac or Hades
No fixed run timer, but difficulty scales continuously with time spent: enemies get stronger the longer you stay, so pace is part of strategy
Items are almost all passive and stack without a cap, creating emergent build chaos rather than fixed builds
Looping the game (continuing past the final boss) and the Void, Lunar and Eclipse layers give it a long endgame
Lunar items are deliberate risk/reward trade-offs that can cost you mobility or your whole inventory
Teleporter boss fights plus an open-ended hunt for chests, shrines and multishops in each stage
tedious_or_disliked: Hunting for the hidden teleporter on each stage can eat time; many players rely on the indicator settings
Shrine of Chance and other gambling objects feel punishing with low success rates
Unlocking all artifacts, skins and challenges can be grindy and repeats risky deaths
Long late-game loops where screens are unreadable and performance drops
Some find the game never clicks; a negative reviewer said they never felt like continuing despite good music, visuals and pacing
divisive_points: Difficulty and one-shot deaths: lovers call it fair rule-mastery, others call it cheap
Simple environments and visuals: praised as gameplay-first clarity by some, called tech-demo-like by others
Whether the paid expansions (especially Seekers of the Storm) improved or diluted the game
Whether to recommend the game at all, given the Gearbox/Take-Two EULA, with many positive-playtime reviewers voting down on principle
community.reception_notes: Early access launched March 2019 and drew over 650,000 players in week one and over a million sales in the first month; PC sales passed 4 million by March 2021 (Wikipedia). Full 1.0 release was Aug 11, 2020, consoles Oct 2020, PS5/Xbox Series in Aug 2024. SteamSpy estimates 5-10 million owners and the steam-revenue-calculator estimate is around $264M gross / $78M net (rough Boxleiter-method estimates, not audited). Gearbox acquired the IP in Nov 2022 and Hopoo Games went on hiatus in Sept 2024 when key developers joined Valve. Steam now shows wave of negative reviews tied to a newer EULA with mandatory arbitration and to multiplayer desync, even from players with hundreds of hours. Some sources saw web-search limits: OpenCritic page could not be fetched, so the opencritic score is null (Wikipedia mentions 93% recommend). Steam store page fetch showed 95% of 163k reviews, apparently a cached older number; local data shows 93.8% of 353k.
